target_customer: State and local governments (code enforcement, housing and community development departments)
problem: City departments keep housing and property data in closed silos, so they cannot find unsafe or blighted properties early.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription sold to local governments

founders.name: Andrew Kieve
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder/CEO on the YC page; no bio there.

founders.name: Nico Tejera
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder/CTO on the YC page; no bio there.

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating messy, closed municipal data systems and building predictive models for vacant properties is standard engineering with hard integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Once a city's data is integrated and staff trained, switching is costly, but sales cycles are slow and no sourced evidence of a moat beyond integrations.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying it; the company is listed active.

market_need_then: A 2017 Route Fifty article on a High Point, NC deployment describes cities using it to predict problems with vacant properties and break down departmental silos, showing real municipal demand.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand coverage; search results confuse it with Tolemy Bio. Government customers buy on references more than brand.

outcome_analysis: Tolemi sells its BuildingBlocks platform to city governments such as High Point, NC and Sherman, TX, and the YC page lists it as active with about 20 people. Funding is unclear because aggregators disagree, so no strong claim about its growth can be made. Government sales cycles are long, but no sourced evidence of failure or exit was found.
notes: Company website fetch was blocked by a rate-limited domain safety check, so the site was not read. Funding is unverified: Seedtable shows 120K seed in 2017-03 with Canyon Creek Capital and YC, Startupintros shows 3M seed in 2017-12, Parsers.vc shows 3.06M, Neuronfeed shows 4M, CB Insights shows 630K over four rounds under former name OpportunitySpace. All aggregators, so no round recorded. No dated competitor source found near the batch, so the list is empty.
